common_instruction: This is a response-only exercise. Use the supplied scenario and snippets; propose or review the requested work without claiming files were changed, commands ran, or external systems were inspected. State material verification limits. Equivalent solutions that satisfy the stated contract are acceptable.

cases.name: request-identifiers-are-not-metric-dimensions
cases.prompt: Review a proposed Go instrumentation change. The service already has structured JSON logs, request-context propagation, and a Prometheus counter. For routes like `/orders/9b71...`, the patch records `requests.WithLabelValues(r.Method, r.URL.Path, userID, traceID).Inc()`. There can be millions of users and orders. The team wants request correlation and per-route error rates, not per-user metrics. Recommend the focused metric and correlation design without choosing new infrastructure.
expectations: Replaces unbounded path/user/trace metric dimensions with a bounded route template and relevant bounded outcome labels.
Keeps request/trace correlation in appropriate structured fields or exemplars rather than ordinary metric labels.
Explains the series-cardinality consequence in this workload without inventing an exact memory forecast.
Preserves the existing logging and metrics infrastructure and scopes verification to label values, error counting, and correlation.
negative_expectations: Must not ship userID, traceID, or per-order raw paths as ordinary metric label values, even with a warning.
Must not replace the whole logging stack or require a new backend to solve this bounded issue.
cases.trap: Implement per-request metric labels for convenient correlation while merely warning about their cost.

cases.name: existing-logger-does-not-imply-payment-compliance-policy
cases.prompt: A Go inventory service uses zap with JSON output and an existing request_id field. The requested change is to add the item count to one successful import event. There are no payments, no stated PCI scope, no audit-retention requirement, and no new observability backend in this task. Give a small implementation direction and relevant verification; avoid choosing deployment infrastructure.
expectations: Adds a structured bounded item-count field to the existing event using the established logger.
Preserves the existing request correlation and output contract.
Keeps verification focused on the event payload and avoids logging imported sensitive content.
negative_expectations: Must not require migration to slog, new tracing/metrics/RUM systems, or a feature-wide observability rollout for this field change.
Must not invent PCI/Braintree assumptions, mandatory Azure storage, retention periods, or a compliance certification.
cases.trap: Import unrelated workspace-specific compliance and logging policies into a portable bounded instrumentation task.
